name: Forager's crop
description: A forager's pouch, mouth open, standing on the plate with nothing in front of it. The hide is dyed with earth — a rust body under a warmer lit face pushed up-left, so the shaded side is the base showing rather than a shadow laid over it — with a hand-stitched seam of ochre dashes riding the lower curve and the rolled edge picked out in the same ochre. The silhouette is not an ellipse: one generator makes the outline, the body and the lit face at three scales so all three share a shape, and that shape pinches under the mouth where a cord would gather it, sags a little wider low down where the weight sits, and carries two soft lumps so the edge reads as hide. The mouth is a hole and is drawn as one: a linear gradient down the shaft, lit rust at the top where the far wall's inside catches the light, falling through soil to ink where the bag goes deep. That is the one place this shelf's usual rule is turned round on purpose — everywhere else a dark ellipse on a bright body is an eye or a mouth and is banned — so the two things that stop it reading as a pupil carry the whole drawing: the opening is nearly as wide as the bag rather than a disc floating in the middle of it, and the rolled edge rings it in ochre, lit up-left and shaded down-right, which no eye has. A pale tanned version came first and was a sack from anywhere; the dye, the seam and the bound edge are what make it a thing somebody in this world made. Deep $rust is otherwise only an accent in this library, so a body this size in it belongs to nothing else on the shelf, and the amber crowd (ss.relic.mine, ss.relic.digest) stays well clear. ss.relic.tithe is the other open container and is a shallow dish of red seen from above where this is a deep bag seen from the front.

glyph.description: Plate off, object only — the silhouette a collection shows for an entry not yet met.
